items: Progress briefing for Lauren Heath and the leadership team
Prepared by Michael Morris, Ashcombe Advisory Partners
Program start: {{fact:f:E-2018-001.start}}
Status: early phase, roughly one quarter of the way through
The foundations are in: we have heard how the company is read today and agreed how it wants to be read.
Listening is done, from your leadership and from analysts who cover the sector.
Drafting of the core messages is under way and on the plan we set at kickoff.
Nothing on the calendar has been missed, and no message has had to be written against the clock.
One core narrative that says plainly what the company is and where it is going.
Three supporting messages, each carried by concrete proof points rather than adjectives.
Written in the company's own register, so it reads as the company speaking and not as an agency writing on its behalf.
A first full draft is close and will come to your team for comment.

blocks.text: The team and how we work

items: Michael Morris leads the engagement and owns the strategy and the sensitive calls.
Laura Bradley carries the drafting and keeps the schedule and the moving parts in order.
Michelle Black runs the announcement timelines and the approvals that sit behind them.
The work moves mostly by email and short calls, with a working session when a decision needs the room.
Timely sign-off: the later materials all build on the core narrative, so its review sets the pace.
One voice to the market: several people speak for the company, and the messaging holds only if they use the same language.
A live announcement in the window: if a result or a deal lands mid-program, we will want to test the messaging against it first.
Send the core-narrative draft to your team for comment as soon as it is ready.
Book the review so the second half of the program can start on time.
Line up a short session with your spokespeople once the supporting messages are drafted.
